title: Monthly Report – October 2026: Human Rights Situation in Iran
content:
Executions and Death Sentences

During October, 71 male prisoners were executed by hanging in prisons across Iran. Of those executed, 30 had been convicted of murder, while 26 were executed on drug-related charges. One prisoner was executed on a rape charge, and the charges against eight others remain unknown.

Of particular concern, however, is the continued use of the death penalty for political or security-related offenses, a practice that has intensified following the recent wars. During the month, two individuals, including an Iraqi national, were executed on espionage charges. Four others were executed on political charges under the charge of moharebeh (enmity against God).
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: January 2026 Protests: Shahab Zohdi Sentenced to Death for the Second Time
content:
According to HRANA, Shahab Zohdi has once again been sentenced to death.

A source close to Zohdi’s family confirmed the news to HRANA, stating: “Following a retrial of Mr. Zohdi’s case, Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Abolghasem Salavati, sentenced him to death for the second time.”

In August 2026, Branch 9 of the Supreme Court overturned Shahab Zohdi’s death sentence and referred his case to Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court for retrial.

In February 2026, Zohdi was initially sentenced to death by Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Abolghasem Salavati, in connection with a case involving a fire at the “185 Shahid Mahmoud Kaveh” Basij base in eastern Tehran.

During the nationwide protests of January 2026, Zohdi and four other prisoners, Mohammadamin Biglari, Shahin Vahedparast Kalour, Amirhossein Hatami, and Ali Fahim, were prosecuted and arrested in a joint case related to the fire at the “185 Shahid Mahmoud Kaveh” Basij base in eastern Tehran on the evening of January 8, 2026.
snippet: According to HRANA, Shahab Zohdi has once again been sentenced to death.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Appeals Court Upholds Prison Sentence and Other Penalties Against Baha’i Citizen Noyan Hejazi
content:
According to HRANA, the prison sentence and other penalties imposed on Noyan Hejazi have been upheld on appeal.

According to the appellate court ruling, Hejazi’s conviction for what authorities described as “promoting the Baha’i faith” was upheld, along with a fine of 122 million and 501 thousand tomans and deprivation of social rights for 10 years and one day. His sentence of seven months and 16 days of discretionary imprisonment on the charge of “propaganda against the Islamic Republic of Iran through cyberspace” was also upheld. The appellate ruling was issued on October 5, 2026, and declared final.

The ruling was signed by Shoja Zoghi and Ebrahim Arab Kheradmardi, judicial advisers to Branch 9 of the Mazandaran Province Court of Appeals.

On May 26, 2026, Noyan Hejazi had been sentenced to the aforementioned penalties by Branch 102 of the Criminal Court II of Juybar.
snippet: According to HRANA, the prison sentence and other penalties imposed on Noyan Hejazi have been upheld on appeal.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Six Sunni Citizens Arrested by IRGC Intelligence Forces in Shavur
content:
According to HRANA, six Sunni citizens were arrested in Shavur on Thursday, October 29, 2026. Five of the detainees have been identified as Hossein Navaseri, 20, Ali Doshi, 25, Ali Shoveyhi, Amin Shoveyhi, 20, and Javad Kanani, 27. The identity of the sixth detainee remains under investigation.

According to information received by HRANA, IRGC intelligence agents raided the homes of these citizens at approximately 1:30 a.m. without presenting judicial warrants. After searching the premises, the agents arrested them.

During the raids, the agents reportedly used violence, creating an atmosphere of fear and intimidation among family members. Several relatives of the detainees were also physically assaulted and beaten.

At the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the reasons for their arrests, the charges brought against them, or their whereabouts.

Shavur is located in Karkheh County, Khuzestan Province, approximately 15 kilometers from the city of Shush.

title: January 2026 Protests: Milad Ebrahimi Sentenced to Prison and Fine
content:
According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, Milad Ebrahimi has been sentenced to imprisonment and a fine.

The report states that Branch 101 of the Criminal Court II of Kamyaran issued a verdict against Ebrahimi, which was communicated to him on Sunday, October 25, 2026. Under the ruling, he was sentenced to one year of discretionary imprisonment and a fine of 400 million tomans on the charge of “disrupting public order.”

The court hearing concerning the charges against Ebrahimi was held in October of this year before the same judicial branch.

On February 1, 2026, Milad Ebrahimi was arrested alongside his brother, Hamed Ebrahimi, by security forces in Kamyaran and transferred to the Ministry of Intelligence’s detention facility in Sanandaj. His arrest took place while he was recovering at home from injuries sustained during the protests in Kamyaran on the evening of January 8, 2026. During those protests, he had been struck in the lower back by live ammunition and subsequently underwent surgery at a hospital in Sanandaj.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, Milad Ebrahimi has been sentenced to imprisonment and a fine.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Supreme Court Upholds Death Sentence Against Mohammad Naderi
content:
According to HRANA, the death sentence against Mohammad Naderi has been upheld. Based on information received by HRANA, the Supreme Court has upheld the death sentence of Mohammad Naderi, who is currently held in Ward 3, Hall 37 of Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj. He had previously been sentenced to death by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court on charges of “espionage.”

An informed source close to Naderi’s family told HRANA: “Using Starlink satellite internet, photographing certain locations, and sending images to media outlets abroad were among the allegations brought against him and served as the basis for his death sentence.”

Naderi was arrested by security forces in Tehran on March 17, 2026, amid war-related security developments, and transferred to the Greater Tehran Prison. He was subsequently transferred to Ghezel Hesar Prison in October of this year.

title: January 2026 Protests: Omran Amani Sentenced to Death
content:
According to HRANA, Omran Amani has been sentenced to death. The sentence was issued by Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Iman Afshari, and communicated to Amani in prison on Saturday, October 24, 2026. Under the ruling, the 21-year-old was sentenced to death on charges of “moharebeh” (waging war against God).

Omran Amani, a native of Kurdistan Province, had previously moved to Tehran in search of employment. He was arrested by security forces during the nationwide protests of January 2026 and is currently held in the Greater Tehran Prison.

HRANA is investigating further details regarding the specific allegations underlying the charge against him and the legal proceedings in his case.

title: Tehran Revolutionary Court Sentences Three More Detainees from January Protests to Death
content:
Based on information received by HRANA, Amirreza Rezaei, Vahid Ghahremani, and a cleric named Mehdi (surname unknown) were sentenced to death by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. Among the charges brought against the three individuals in this case is allegedly carrying out operations on behalf of Israel. The death sentences were communicated to them in prison on Monday, October 26, 2026.

Mehdi, another defendant in the case, is a cleric and a former member of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). He has also been sentenced to death by the Special Clerical Court in a separate case on charges of “apostasy.” Consequently, two death sentences have been issued against him in two separate cases.

The three individuals were arrested separately by security forces during the nationwide protests of January 2026.

On Wednesday, October 28, 2026, they were transferred from the Greater Tehran Prison to Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj.

title: Nabi Omidi Sentenced to Nine Years in Prison Following Appeals Court Ruling
content:
According to HRANA, the sentence issued against Nabi Omidi has been upheld in full on appeal.

According to information obtained by HRANA, Branch One of the Ilam Province Court of Appeals upheld Mr. Omidi’s nine-year prison sentence on charges including “acting against national security,” “propaganda against the regime,” and “participation in protests.” Under Article 134 of the Islamic Penal Code, five years of this sentence will be enforceable.

Mr. Omidi had previously been sentenced by judicial authorities to imprisonment, a travel ban prohibiting him from leaving the country, and a ban on entering Malekshahi County. He was also dismissed from Payame Noor University in Ilam in January 2026, amid nationwide protests.

Among the allegations cited against Mr. Omidi was “standing alongside the people of Malekshahi during the January protests.”

In January 2026, amid nationwide protests, Nabi Omidi was arrested by security forces in Ilam and subsequently transferred to the city’s prison.

The report provides no further details about the case, including the judicial authorities responsible for issuing the imprisonment and dismissal orders or the full range of charges brought against him.
snippet: According to HRANA, the sentence issued against Nabi Omidi has been upheld in full on appeal.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Amin Ghanbari Sentenced to 20 Years in Prison
content:
According to HRANA, citing Modara, Amin Ghanbari has been sentenced to imprisonment.

According to the report, Branch One of the Semnan Revolutionary Court sentenced Mr. Ghanbari to 20 years in prison on charges of “engaging in media activities against the Islamic Republic,” “assembly and collusion against national security,” “propaganda against the regime,” “supporting the Pahlavi and those killed during the January 2026 protests,” and “insulting the founder of the Islamic Republic.”

Ghanbari was arrested by security forces outside his home in April–May 2026.

The report provides no further information regarding the details of his case, the evidence supporting the charges brought against him, or his current place of detention.

Amin Ghanbari, a resident of Semnan, previously managed the Telegram channel “Payam-Goo-ye Semnan” (Semnan Messenger).
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Modara, Amin Ghanbari has been sentenced to imprisonment.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: January 2026 Protests: Supreme Court Upholds Death Sentence of Arman Marefati
content:
According to HRANA, the death sentence of Arman Marefati, one of those arrested during the January 2026 protests, has been upheld.

According to information obtained by HRANA, the Supreme Court upheld the death sentence of Arman Marefati, who is currently held in Ward 3, Hall 37 of Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj. He had previously been sentenced to death by Judge Abolghasem Salavati, head of Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, on charges including participation in operational activities against national security, entering religious premises with the intent to cause destruction, and involvement in setting fire to a mosque and a religious seminary.

It is worth noting that the death sentences of two other prisoners, Mehrdad Mohammadinia and Ashkan Maleki, who were co-defendants in the same case as Arman Marefati, were carried out in June 2026. The two prisoners had been sentenced to death on charges of “collaboration with the Zionist regime and hostile governments,” “creating insecurity and public fear,” “destruction and arson of public property,” and “participation in operational activities against national security.”
snippet: According to HRANA, the death sentence of Arman Marefati, one of those arrested during the January 2026 protests, has been upheld.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Mahshahr Writer Elias Ghanavati Lari Remains in Detention, Whereabouts Unknown
content:
According to HRANA, citing the Iranian Writers’ Association, Elias Ghanavati Lari, a writer and poet from Mahshahr, remains in detention.

According to the report, Mr. Ghanavati Lari was arrested by security forces on Wednesday, October 21, 2026.

Twelve days after his arrest, no information has been obtained regarding his condition or whereabouts.

His published works include the book Two Absurd Plays to Gather Dust and the article Proudhon and Marx at the Scene of the Theft.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing the Iranian Writers’ Association, Elias Ghanavati Lari, a writer and poet from Mahshahr, remains in detention.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: One Prisoner Executed at Adelabad Prison in Shiraz
content:
According to HRANA, a prisoner was executed at Adelabad Prison in Shiraz. HRANA has identified the prisoner, who was hanged at dawn on Sunday, November 1, as Iman Ashraf.

According to information obtained by HRANA, Mr. Ashraf had previously been arrested on a murder charge and subsequently sentenced to death by a criminal court.

As of the time of this report, the execution has not been officially announced by prison authorities or other relevant institutions.

Between October 10, 2025, and October 8, 2026, HRANA documented at least 2,003 executions across Iran, based on 1,857 reports, representing an increase of approximately 29% compared to the previous reporting period. During the same period, HRANA also documented 230 death sentences. For more detailed statistics and analysis of executions in Iran, read HRANA’s latest comprehensive report.
snippet: According to HRANA, a prisoner was executed at Adelabad Prison in Shiraz. HRANA has identified the prisoner, who was hanged at dawn on Sunday, November 1, as Iman Ashraf.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Peyvand and Borna Naeimi, Two Baha’i Citizens, Sentenced to a Combined Prison Term of More Than 20 Years
content:
According to HRANA, citing IranWire, Peyvand Naeimi and Borna Naeimi have been sentenced to a combined prison term of more than 20 years.

The report states that Branch 5 of the Kerman Revolutionary Court issued the sentences against the two Baha’i citizens, who are cousins. Under the verdicts, Peyvand Naeimi was sentenced to 12 years, six months, and one day in prison, while Borna Naeimi was sentenced to eight years.

No precise information is currently available regarding the charges that led to the prison sentences against these two citizens.

Previously, a source familiar with the situation of the two Baha’i citizens told HRANA that Peyvand Naeimi’s court hearing had been scheduled for September 18, 2026. Borna Naeimi was also tried via video conference by the Kerman Revolutionary Court on May 25, 2026, on charges including “acting against national security and forming a group with the intention of overthrowing the government.”
snippet: According to HRANA, citing IranWire, Peyvand Naeimi and Borna Naeimi have been sentenced to a combined prison term of more than 20 years.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Two Citizens Arrested by Security Forces in Oshnavieh
content:
According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, two residents of Shahvaneh village in Oshnavieh County were arrested by security forces.

The individuals have been identified as Kumar Royan, 22, and Sadreddin Esmailzadeh, 34, both residents of Shahvaneh village.

According to the report, on Saturday, October 31, 2026, agents of the Ministry of Intelligence entered Kumar Royan’s workplace and arrested him without presenting a judicial warrant. Similarly, on Sunday, November 1, 2026, Sadreddin Esmailzadeh was arrested without a judicial warrant after security forces raided his home.

At the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the reasons for their arrests, their whereabouts, or the charges brought against them.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, two residents of Shahvaneh village in Oshnavieh County were arrested by security forces.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Danial Dabiri Sentenced to Five Years in Prison
content:
According to HRANA, Danial Dabiri, who was arrested during the protests in January of this year, has been sentenced to prison.

Based on information received by HRANA, Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Iman Afshari, sentenced Dabiri to five years in prison on the charge of “assembly and collusion against national security.”

Danial Dabiri, a 23-year-old citizen, was arrested in Tehran on January 4, 2026, during nationwide protests. He was subsequently transferred to Greater Tehran Prison.
